data_requests.item: Existing compressor/cooling, recovery and receiving-duty basis
where: site records: Existing actual compressor type/cooling arrangement and performance, available thermal quantity/temperature and load/run schedule, existing recovery/coverage and receiving heat duty/temperature/time/seasonality, displaced energy and quality/material/cooling/ventilation/backpressure/control constraints, with exact units/source/owner/revision/availability.

a walkdown: Only if an applicable question remains after reviewing existing records, agree safe additional observations with the responsible engineer; no mandatory new meter, field test, operating change or equipment replacement.
data_requests.how: S11 printed58-59 describes heat fractions and different air-cooled/water-cooled arrangements. Electrical input converted to heat and a recovered fraction of available thermal energy are not electrical savings or a useful site duty. Establish compatible temperatures, coincident demand and source/configuration first; the source says this heat is usually insufficient for direct steam production. Nearby load or long hours alone is insufficient. Retain required compressor cooling, ventilation/backpressure, water-quality/material and control constraints and added fan/exchanger effects. Acknowledge suitable existing recovery or nonapplicability; missing coverage remains conditional rather than a forced field test or new exchanger.

questions.decision_rule: Review actual compressor/cooling performance, existing recovery and useful receiving duty, temperature, timing and operating/material/control constraints with the responsible specialist. Do not infer feasibility, useful output or a required retrofit from proximity/run hours or source heat percentages. Suitable existing recovery or nonapplicability may be acknowledged; unresolved source, service, units or duty remains explicit. No heat-recovery design, steam promise or site savings is produced.

typical_benefit.wording: "As much as 80 to 93 percent of the electrical energy" becomes heat; recovery "anywhere from 50 to 90 percent of this".
source_titles: S11: Improving Compressed Air System Performance: A Sourcebook for Industry, 3rd ed. (DOE + Compressed Air Challenge)

questions.limits: Source review: S11 printed58-59/PDF63-64, full heat-recovery context. Its80-93% electrical-to-heat fraction and50-90% recovery of available thermal energy are contextual source figures, not electricity or site savings; compressor/cooling/design and compatible receiving duty matter. The worked example omits additional fan power and warns of exchanger effects. Actual energy displacement and ventilation/cooling/quality constraints require review.
